metadata.methodology: Symptoms extracted only when explicitly mentioned by at least 2 authoritative medical sources. Frequency classified based on language used by sources (e.g., 'common', 'may also have', 'in severe cases'). Synonyms normalized per specification.
authoritative_sources_consulted: CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)
quality_rules_applied: Each symptom confirmed by minimum 2 authoritative sources
No symptoms inferred - only explicitly mentioned symptoms included
False negatives preferred over false positives

diseases.description: An infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, affecting primarily the respiratory system.
A common viral infection of the nose and throat (upper respiratory tract).
An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus.
diseases.pathogen: Streptococcus pneumoniae (most common bacterial), viruses, fungi
diseases.incubation_period: varies by pathogen (1-3 days for bacterial, 1-7 days for viral)

diseases.description: A bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs but can spread to other parts of the body.
A life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through the bites of infected Anopheles mosquitoes.
diseases.pathogen: Plasmodium parasites (P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale, P. knowlesi)

diseases.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing a severe flu-like illness, sometimes progressing to potentially lethal complications.

diseases.description: A chronic infection caused by the human immunodeficiency virus that attacks the immune system, potentially leading to AIDS if untreated.
diseases.incubation_period: 2-4 weeks (acute phase); can remain asymptomatic for years

diseases.description: A viral infection that attacks the liver and can cause both acute and chronic disease.
Inflammation of the membranes (meninges) surrounding the brain and spinal cord, most commonly caused by bacterial or viral infection.
diseases.pathogen: Neisseria meningitidis (bacterial), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, viruses

diseases.description: A life-threatening systemic infection caused by the bacterium Salmonella Typhi.
A highly contagious liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus.
A liver disease caused by the hepatitis C virus, leading to acute and chronic infection.
A mosquito-borne viral disease characterized by sudden onset of fever and severe joint pain.
A highly contagious disease caused by the varicella-zoster virus (VZV), known for its characteristic blister-like rash.
A highly contagious viral disease that can lead to serious complications.
A viral infection that primarily affects saliva-producing (salivary) glands that are situated near your ears.
A deadly viral disease that causes progressive and fatal inflammation of the brain and spinal cord.

symptoms.symptom: pain or tingling at bite site

diseases.description: A bacterial disease that affects humans and animals, transmitted primarily through water contaminated with animal urine.
transmission: contact with contaminated water, soil, or animal urine

diseases.description: An infectious illness commonly caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), primarily spreading through saliva.
An acute diarrhoeal infection caused by ingestion of food or water contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
A parasitic infection of the colon with the amoeba Entamoeba histolytica.
A diarrheal disease caused by the microscopic parasite Giardia duodenalis.
An intestinal infection caused by a family of bacteria known as Shigella.
A common bacterial disease that affects the intestinal tract, commonly caused by contaminated food.
A bacterial infection transmitted from animals to humans, primarily via unpasteurized dairy products.
A serious illness caused by Clostridium tetani bacteria, leading to painful muscle contractions, particularly in the jaw and neck.
transmission: contamination of wounds with soil/feces containing spores

diseases.description: A highly contagious respiratory tract infection that is easily preventable by vaccine, known for its severe hacking cough.
A bacterial illness that develops in some people who have strep throat, featuring a bright red rash.
A tick-borne illness caused by the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi.
A sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum, progressing through distinct stages if untreated.
A sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, affecting mucous membranes of the reproductive tract, mouth, throat, eyes, and rectum.
A common sexually transmitted infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, often asymptomatic but can cause serious reproductive complications.

symptoms.symptom: bleeding between periods or after sex (in women)

diseases.description: A common sexually transmitted infection caused by herpes simplex virus, characterized by recurrent painful genital sores.

symptoms.symptom: painful blisters or sores on genitals

diseases.description: The most common sexually transmitted infection, with certain types causing genital warts and others associated with cancers.
An infection of the female upper genital tract, including the uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries, usually caused by sexually transmitted bacteria.

symptoms.symptom: bleeding between periods or after sex

diseases.pathogen: Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae (most common), mixed polymicrobial

diseases.description: An infection of the inner lining of the heart chambers and valves (endocardium), usually caused by bacteria.
diseases.pathogen: Staphylococcus aureus (most common), Streptococcus viridans, Enterococci

diseases.description: A highly contagious illness caused by norovirus, the leading cause of vomiting and diarrhea from acute gastroenteritis.
A highly contagious viral infection that is the most common cause of severe diarrhoeal disease among infants and young children worldwide.
A common respiratory virus that usually causes mild, cold-like symptoms but can be serious for infants and older adults.
A serious bacterial infection affecting the mucous membranes of the throat and nose, producing a thick grey-white coating.
transmission: direct contact with infected skin lesions

diseases.description: A highly infectious viral disease that mainly affects young children and can cause irreversible paralysis.
A mosquito-borne viral infection that is the leading cause of viral encephalitis in Asia.
A mite-borne infectious disease caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, transmitted through the bite of infected larval mites (chiggers).
A mosquito-borne viral disease usually causing mild illness in adults but associated with serious birth defects when contracted during pregnancy.
An acute viral hemorrhagic disease transmitted by infected mosquitoes, with a high case-fatality ratio in severe cases.

symptoms.symptom: bleeding (from mouth, nose, eyes, or stomach)

diseases.description: A life-threatening infectious disease caused by Yersinia pestis, transmitted through flea bites or contact with infected animals.
A parasitic disease caused by Toxoplasma gondii, usually asymptomatic in healthy individuals but dangerous for immunocompromised patients and during pregnancy.
A common herpesvirus infection, usually asymptomatic in healthy individuals but can cause serious illness in immunocompromised patients and newborns.
transmission: body fluids (saliva, blood, urine, breast milk)

diseases.description: A fungal infection caused by Candida species, most commonly affecting the mouth (oral thrush), genitals, and skin.
